title: Quiz: Acceptance Sampling Plans and OC Curves

questions.text: A single sampling plan is defined by parameters (n, c). If the number of defectives d found in the sample satisfies d > c, what decision is made?
questions.explanation: In a single sampling plan, the lot is rejected whenever the observed number of defectives d exceeds the acceptance number c. If d ≤ c, the lot is accepted.

questions.text: Producer risk α is defined as the probability of:
options: Rejecting a lot whose incoming defect rate equals the AQL
Accepting a lot whose incoming defect rate equals the LTPD
Accepting a lot whose incoming defect rate equals the AQL
Rejecting a lot whose incoming defect rate equals the LTPD
questions.explanation: Producer risk α is the probability of falsely rejecting a good lot — one with an incoming defect rate at the AQL. It represents the fraction of acceptable lots that the sampling plan will erroneously turn away.

questions.text: For a sampling plan (n=100, c=2), you compute P(accept | p=0.05) using the binomial CDF. Which expression is correct?
questions.explanation: P(accept) = P(D ≤ c | n, p) = sum from d=0 to c of C(n,d) × p^d × (1-p)^(n-d). In scipy, this equals binom.cdf(c, n, p) = binom.cdf(2, 100, 0.05).

questions.text: Two sampling plans have the same AQL and LTPD. Plan A has n=50, c=1; Plan B has n=150, c=3. Which statement best describes the difference in their OC curves?
options: Plan B has a steeper OC curve and better discriminates between good and bad lots
Plan A has a steeper OC curve because a smaller acceptance number is more stringent
Both plans have identical OC curves since AQL and LTPD are the same
Plan B accepts more bad lots because c=3 is larger than c=1
questions.explanation: Increasing n (sample size) makes the OC curve steeper, improving discrimination. Plan B with n=150 has a much steeper curve than Plan A with n=50, simultaneously reducing both α and β compared to Plan A, at the cost of a larger inspection sample.

questions.text: Acceptance sampling improves the quality of the items inside an accepted lot.
questions.explanation: Acceptance sampling is a decision tool — it decides whether to accept or reject a lot based on sample evidence. It does not improve the quality of individual units inside an accepted lot. Quality improvement requires process control and elimination of root causes of defects.
